title: The closure-normalized relative transpose agrees with the ambient immersion transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow T$ be an immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, factored as $s=v\circ c$ with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the two small sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $F_\tau=v_{\tau,!}c_{\tau,*}$ and $J_\tau=Rc_\tau^!v_\tau^*$ for $\tau=e,p$, with the pasted adjunctions $F_\tau\dashv J_\tau$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], where the two open extensions are those of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $\bar S$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $s$, with $s=i\circ u$, $u:S\hookrightarrow\bar S$ open and $i:\bar S\hookrightarrow T$ closed [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Here $\bar S=\operatorname{SIm}(s)$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to s_*\mathcal O_S)$; $i$ is its image inclusion and $u$ its canonical factor map. These immersions into the Noetherian scheme $T$ are quasi-compact, so this ideal is the kernel itself. Write $E_\tau=i_{\tau,*}u_{\tau,!}$.

Let $q_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}E_\tau$ be the identity-normalized termwise extension identifications [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison, lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence], and identify $J_e$ with the etale compact-support right adjoint $s^\times$ by the adjunction conjugate of $q_e$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ and $U_W=R\nu_{W,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with unit $\eta_W$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and $G_s=C_Ss^\times U_T$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ let
$$\Delta_L=v_{p,!}(\delta_{c,L})o_{v,c_{e,*}L},\qquad B_L=i_{p,*}(o_{u,L})\delta_{i,u_{e,!}L}$$
use the canonical counit-mate closed comparison and open comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Suppose $q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L})$ for every such $L$.

Let $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with $H=J_eM\in D^+(S_e,A)$. Suppose a natural isomorphism $\gamma_M:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}J_pC_TM$ satisfies
$$\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma_M)\Delta_H=C_T(\epsilon^e_M),$$
where $\epsilon^\tau$ are the pasted counits. For every $h:F_pC_SL\to C_TM$, there is a unique $h_0:F_eL\to M$ with $h\Delta_L=C_T(h_0)$. Put $g_0=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0):L\to H$ and $\rho_M=C_S(s^\times(\eta_{T,M}))$, under the fixed identification $J_e\cong s^\times$. Then
$$\operatorname{adj}_{F_p\dashv J_p}(h)=\gamma_MC_S(g_0),\qquad
\Phi_{L,C_TM}(h q_{p,C_SL}^{-1})=\rho_MC_S(g_0),$$
where $\Phi$ is the chosen-closure-compactification Hom bijection of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. More explicitly, for $z:E_pC_SL\to C_TM$ this normalization is
$$\Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=C_S\left(\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv s^\times}\left(U_T(zB_L)\eta_{T,E_eL}\right)\right).$$
Consequently $\theta_M=\rho_M\gamma_M^{-1}:J_pC_TM\xrightarrow{\sim}G_s(C_TM)$ identifies the ambient and comparison-class Hom bijections, hence all their defined unit and counit maps. The same conclusion holds for every test object isomorphic to $C_SL$ with $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ and is independent of the chosen witness. It is natural in $M,L$ and in identity-normalized changes of factorization that commute with $\Delta$. No adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects is asserted.

proof.text: Use the closure-adjoint realization for exactness of $F_e,E_e$, preservation of lower bounds and the fixed conjugate identification $J_e\cong s^\times$. Thus $F_eL,E_eL,F_eH$ and $M$ are in $D^+$. The closure comparison square gives the natural isomorphisms $\Delta,B$ with exactly the displayed closed-mate/open normalizations. These are the hypotheses on the forward functors needed below.

source.place: Second paragraph; old Step 1, using existing forward exactness and comparison statements.

proof.text: Apply the counit/closure-unit calculus with the ordinary derived categories, full subcategories $\mathcal A_0=D^+(S_e,A)$, $\mathcal B_0=D^+(T_e,A)$, $\mathcal Q_0=D^+(T_p,A)$, $C_S=\nu_S^*$, $C_T=\nu_T^*$, $U=U_T$ the bounded-below derived direct image on $\mathcal Q_0$ and $\eta$ its unit on $\mathcal B_0$; $F_e,E_e$ preserve $D^+$ by Step 1. Site comparison supplies this unit, full faithfulness on $\mathcal B_0$ and invertibility of $\eta_{T,M}$. Its transported $E_e$ adjunction is precisely the fixed $s^\times$ adjunction. The specified chosen-closure Hom formula is the $\Phi$ of that calculus. Consequently there is a unique $h_0$, and both transposes are respectively $\gamma_MC_S(g_0)$ and $\rho_MC_S(g_0)$, with $\rho_M$ invertible.

source.place: Second paragraph; old Steps 2–5, applied with the supplied closure square and normalized counit.

proof.text: Put $\theta_M=\rho_M\gamma_M^{-1}$; the two formulas give $\Phi(hq_p^{-1})=\theta_M\operatorname{adj}_p(h)$. Apply relative Hom witness transport with $F=F_p$, $E=E_p$, $C=C_S$, $J=J_p$ and $G=G_s$, on the full target class of $C_TM$ with the given bounds. The preceding calculation makes $\theta$ natural in $M,L$. Full faithfulness at $S$ is site comparison. The specified relative Hom bijection is witness-independent and natural, and has the prescribed identity-witness value. Therefore the transport lemma identifies it, its inverse, and every defined unit and counit. The isomorphism $\gamma_M:C_SH\cong J_pC_TM$ supplies the counit witness.

source.place: Second paragraph; old Steps 6–7, without enlarging the admissible test class.

proof.text: For a compatible identity-normalized factorization change $r_e,r_p$, the normalized extension identifications give $q\prime_pr_p=q_p$. Identify $J_e$ and $J'_e$ with $s^\times$ by the conjugates of $q_e,q'_e$, so the two etale adjunctions are transported from $E_e\dashv s^\times$ along $q_e,q'_e$. Normalized factorization transpose coherence first gives $q'_er_e=q_e$ (from its squares and the bounded-below faithfulness above, without using the adjunctions); hence the $F'_e$ adjunction is the one transported from $F_e\dashv s^\times$ along $r_e$, as that lemma requires. Apply its remaining conclusions. It gives the transformed lifts, $q\prime_er_e=q_e$, unchanged closure arrows, $\gamma\prime=t\gamma$, and $\theta\prime t=\theta$, with identity and composition laws. This is the asserted naturality for precisely the factorization changes allowed in the statement.
